d01.why: Every player has lived the night of folding then getting no action on kings, and the line makes the viewer need to know why it happened.

d10.why: A tiny scene with a twist ('they read his clock') turns a dry concept into a picture any reg recognises at the table.

d18.why: Opens on the most painful familiar bust-out and then denies it was the culprit, so the viewer must stay to learn what was.

d07.why: Starts from a lost-on-the-river session the viewer has had and moves the blame somewhere unexpected.

d06.why: Funny and specific: the seven-four 'just to feel something' is a confession viewers recognise in themselves and tag friends with.

d03.why: A relatable archetype every home-game player can name and tag, with a quick reversal from 'tough' to 'easy to read'.

d12.why: A then-vs-now arc that mocks the beginner path and withholds the 'third month', though it is a little long.

d16.why: Flips the nit's self-image in two short sentences with a stake, but is closer to a claim than a scene.

d14.why: A personal rivalry with a friend gives a stranger a stake, and 'that isn't luck' sets a question, though the premise may ring false to some.

d19.why: Sets up a visual race the reel must show, but 'watch what' leans on promise more than on a feeling.
